key_insight: HaloBlock improves diffusion LLM decoding by measuring block difficulty and adding adaptive bidirectional halo context to reduce boundary discontinuity and lower hard-token decoding cost.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical inference-time strategy to make dLLMs faster and more accurate on reasoning and code tasks without changing the base model architecture.
method: Compute bidirectional cumulative entropy to estimate decoding difficulty for each block.
Allocate adaptive halo regions on both left and right sides of blocks based on difficulty.
Use the added cross-block context to smooth boundary effects and improve convergence/quality.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on LLaDA-8B-Instruct, Dream-7B-Instruct, and LLaDA-1.5 across mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks, showing consistent accuracy gains and higher inference efficiency.
watch_item: Adaptive halo sizing may increase implementation complexity and inference overhead if block difficulty estimates are noisy or poorly calibrated.
paper_title: HaloBlock: Faster and Better Decoding for Diffusion Large Language Models
